observations.explanation: The paper describes a modular construction workflow with environment, data, and reward components (PDF p. 4), and the appendix specifies the interface and concrete Bash and SQL implementations (PDF pp. 14–19).
The reported SQL results show GPT-4 rising from 9.1% in Single Turn to 73.7% in Try Again (PDF pp. 6–7), supporting the stated example and the qualified claim of gains for some models.
The paper says its current environments cover Bash and SQL and that the CTF dataset has four instances (PDF p. 9); it reiterates both limitations in the appendix (PDF p. 26).

The paper specifies lexical similarity for Bash output grading (PDF pp. 5, 16) and an SQL reward that penalizes incorrect record ordering, with full reward only for the exact ordered result (PDF pp. 5, 19). The question about how these choices affect comparisons with alternative correct outputs is appropriately framed as unresolved.
